gap: No result ChatGPT got states that full-toolhead changers still waste filament at every swap: the Snapmaker U1 keeps all four heads preheated and builds a prime/wiping tower at each colour change, and Prusa says the XL's parked heads must drop to an idle temperature or they ooze, then prime 15–35 mm³ into a wipe tower. Prusa's CORE One+ INDX tools have no heaters of their own, and Prusa says they need 'No waste/prime tower', using 13 mg per change.
standout_why: Cited rivals: 3dtoolchangers.com/printers lists only tool count and change type. 3dprinteray.com/toolchanger-printers mentions the INDX induction coil, the 12 s swap and that the U1 keeps its heads preheated, but says nothing about ooze, idle temperature or a prime tower. Of the top uncited results, slice-lab.com claims 'Since each material keeps its own nozzle, waste is near zero' for full-head changers without mentioning a prime tower, and 3dtoolchangers' INDX-vs-U1 compare page says it can't report waste per change from spec sheets. None explains why parked full heads ooze and still need a tower while INDX tools don't.
decides: If the shopper bought a tool changer to stop wasting filament, this favours the Prusa CORE One+ INDX ($1,999 for 4 tools, $2,249 for 8, assembled). Its parked tools are unheated and need no prime tower. The Snapmaker U1 and Prusa XL+ still print a wipe/prime tower and need idle-temperature settings. The U1 also holds at most four spools per job. Whole-head changers still make sense for a different reason: each head has its own extruder and hotend. A low waste figure is not the reason to pick them.

findings.label: Tool construction and heating
findings.value: Passive tools with 'no motors, no heaters, no wires'. An induction coil on the moving head heats the tool it picks up, and extrusion also stays on the main head.
findings.source_title: Prusa CORE One+ (Gen 2) INDX | Multi-Material Toolchanger 3D Printer
findings.note: Prusa's own words: the head heats 'the passive nozzle in seconds the moment it's picked up'. That parked tools sit unheated follows from their having no heater. Prusa does not say this directly.

findings.label: Prime tower and waste per change
findings.value: No waste/prime tower; 13 mg of material to fully prime per change; about 12 s per change
findings.source_title: Prusa CORE One+ (Gen 2) INDX, Shipping Has Started, Complete Printers Open for Orders
findings.note: Quotes: 'No waste/prime tower as the tool is pre-primed fully' and 'Only 13 milligrams of material to fully prime.' Post dated 2026-08-20. The product page gives about 0.013 g per colour change and says 'you don't need to purge between colors'.

findings.label: US price, maker store
findings.source_title: Prusa CORE One+ (Gen 2) INDX | Multi-Material Toolchanger 3D Printer
findings.note: Prices as shown on the product page. The page adds that tax and shipping are calculated at checkout. The 4-tool printer has docking slots for up to 8 tools.

findings.label: Tool-change mechanism and prime tower
findings.value: Four preheated toolheads, about 5 s per swap. The U1 wipes the nozzle tip at each colour change by building a prime/wiping tower.
findings.note: Snapmaker's footnote counts nozzle clearing, nozzle wiping and flow calibration as waste sources, separate from 'purging'. Its 'up to 85%' less filament than shared-nozzle printers comes from Snapmaker Lab tests and includes the prime tower.

findings.label: Filaments per job
findings.value: Up to 4 spools loaded, one per toolhead. Backup Mode switches to a matching spool when one runs out.
findings.note: 'Each color or material stays loaded in its own dedicated toolhead.'

findings.label: Parked-head ooze handling
findings.value: Ooze prevention must stay on. Without it 'all the extruders will stay at their print temperature during the whole print', which Prusa says causes significant oozing, melt-zone degradation and possible nozzle clogging.
findings.note: Each filament profile's idle temperature takes priority over the ooze-prevention temperature drop.

findings.label: Wipe-tower minimal purge per tool
findings.value: Default 15 mm³ (PLA) and 35 mm³ (other materials). Prusa recommends 35 mm³ per extruder when combining PLA with another material, and up to 70 mm³ for TPU stringing.
findings.note: 'The minimal purge on wipe tower sets the minimum amount of material to prime into the prime tower.'

findings.label: Vortek purge-free condition
findings.value: Six interchangeable induction hotends, each with onboard memory of the filament it last ran, heating up in 8 s. Bambu says purge cleaning can be eliminated when a job uses fewer than seven filaments.
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab H2C: where Multi-Material Vortek System meets engineering precision
findings.note: Bambu blog post dated 2025-11-14. It gives no percentage for purge reduction and doesn't say what happens with more filaments than hotends.
